kind.description: user; api_token (userId is the token's owner); service (the manager's own scheduled or maintenance work); agent; anonymous (no authenticated principal, e.g. a failed sign-in).

action.description: Capability key of the operation (#17) or a lifecycle key such as job.finished or audit.purge.

clientIp.description: Client address as resolved through the trusted reverse proxies.

details.description: Redacted, action-specific details (e.g. rule diffs). Never contains secret values, tokens, file contents or .env values.

errorClass.description: Stable error code or job error class; messages are never recorded.

hash.description: SHA-256 over prevHash and the canonical record.

operationId.description: API operation that was called, if the record stems from a request.

prevHash.description: Hash of the preceding record (tamper evidence).

seq.description: Position in the hash chain; newer records have higher values.

type.description: Resource type (stack, container, volume, image, network, job, user, group, api_token, agent, environment, ...).

features.description: Stable feature-flag keys enabled on this manager.

code.description: Stable snake_case error code; switch on this, not on message.

details.description: Per-field problems, empty when not applicable.

message.description: Human-readable summary. Not stable; do not parse.

requestId.description: Request ID echoed in the X-Request-ID header and the manager logs.

retryable.description: True when repeating the identical request later may succeed.

field.description: Input location, e.g. body.name, query.limit, path.stackId, header.If-Match.

message.description: What is wrong with the value.

commit.description: Source commit the manager was built from.

status.description: Always ok when the process can serve requests.

attempt.description: Dispatch attempt; increases when an interrupted job resumes or a lost command is re-sent.

blockedBy.description: Present while the job is blocked.

cancellable.description: False once the job reached a terminal state.

error.description: Present for failed, partial, cancelled and interrupted jobs.

initiatorTokenId.description: API token used to request the job (audit metadata only).

initiatorUserId.description: User who requested the job (audit metadata only).

kind.description: Job kind from the catalog in docs/architecture/job-engine.md.

locks.description: The job's lock scopes (held while dispatched, running or cancelling).

origin.description: Why the job exists. Audit metadata, not an access-control owner.

startedAt.description: When the current attempt was acknowledged by its executor.

jobId.description: The job holding (or queued first for) the conflicting lock or concurrency slot.

class.description: Stable error class, e.g. agent_offline, authorization_revoked, step_failed, unknown_outcome, journal_lost, cancelled.

recovery.description: What the operator should do next.

seq.description: Monotonic per job; also the SSE event id.

name.description: Resource name; * locks every resource of the scope in the environment; absent for host.

step.description: Current step of the kind's plan.

environmentId.description: Environment of the target when it differs from the job's (migrations).

id.description: Resource identifier within its environment (stack ID, container, volume or network name, image reference, repository ID, absolute path).

items.description: Items on this page (possibly empty, also when nextCursor is present).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; absent on the last page.

total.description: Number of items matching the filters that the caller may see, across all pages. Only on routes that document it.

bearerToken.description: Scoped, expiring API token (#31) sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. A token carries a subset of its owner's capabilities; each request is evaluated as token scope intersected with the owner's current effective permissions.

cookieSession.description: Browser session (#16). Set by POST /api/v1/auth/session as an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie. Unsafe methods authenticated by this cookie must come from the manager's own origin (Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site checks).
cookieSession.name: __Host-dockyard_session

info.description: Public control API of the DockYard manager. All routes live under /api/v1 on the single public origin. Errors use the Error schema with media type application/problem+json. Every operation declares the capability it requires (x-dockyard-capability) and the scope at which it is checked (x-dockyard-scope). Browsers authenticate with the session cookie, other clients with a bearer API token. Conventions, errors, streams and versioning: docs/api/README.md in the DockYard repository.
info.title: DockYard API

post.description: Queued and blocked jobs are cancelled immediately. Running jobs move to cancelling and stop at the next cancellation safe point of their kind; compensating steps (such as restarting containers stopped for a backup) always run. A job that finishes before reaching a safe point keeps its outcome. Repeating the request is harmless. Answers 202 with the job and its URL in Location. 409 job_finished when the job already finished.

get.description: Server-sent events. The first message is `event: job` with the current Job (no id). Then every retained event after Last-Event-ID in order, as `id: <seq>`, `event: <type>` (state, progress, item, log, warning), `data: <JobEvent>`. Comments `: heartbeat` keep the connection alive. The stream closes after the job's terminal events. The event log per job is bounded; replay covers only retained events.
